title: Request filter heuristics and candidate features (Nov 2028)
content:
Summary:
This note proposes a pragmatic filtering/triage heuristic for the flood of customer feedback we see in support, account execs, solutions, and SRE. The goal is to convert noisy asks into a short list of candidate features and experiments (MVP-level) that engineering and product can act on within a 6–10 week cadence.

Scope & goals:
- Focus: product-scope requests tied to inference behavior, API ergonomics, rollout patterns, and observability (excludes pure billing/legal requests).
- Time horizon: prioritize items that can be scoped to an OKR sprint (2–3 sprints).
- Outcome: produce 8–12 candidate features ranked by expected customer impact and implementation cost, plus 3 low-effort probes.

Why this is different:
- Instead of manual labeling by tag or volume alone, we blend three signals: customer severity (customer-reported impact), cross-customer frequency (how many distinct customers report it), and product leverage (how broadly an internal change improves metrics like latency/cost/SLAs).
- We capture 'triage provenance' for each ask so we can trace back to ticket threads for clarifications.

Methodology (heuristics):
1) Signal extraction: pull records from last 9 months across Support (CS tickets), Solutions playbooks, and CSM weekly notes. We exclude single-device complaints unless severity >= P1.
2) Deduplicate: fuzzy-match on request intent (e.g., "dedicated pool latency" vs "dedicated GPU slow startup") and collapse into canonical request statements.
3) Score each canonical request on three axes (0–5):
   - Customer Severity (how badly it blocks revenue/usage)
   - Frequency (distinct customers / organs reporting)
   - Product Leverage (how many upstream subsystems benefit)
4) Compute a composite score: weighted sum (Severity*0.5 + Frequency*0.3 + Leverage*0.2). Use cutoff >= 3.5 for candidate shortlist.
5) Feasibility check: quick engineering sanity check (1–2 engineer-hours) to flag obvious multi-quarter efforts.

Scoring rubric (examples):
- Example A: "Noisy tokenization mismatch for Spanish text causing hallucinations"
  - Severity 3 (some customers affected) / Frequency 2 (few customers) / Leverage 4 (affects embedding & generation pipelines) => composite 3.1 => monitor, move to probe if corroborated.
- Example B: "Route fallback from hosted to dedicated loses KV-cache, spikes latency"
  - Severity 4 / Frequency 4 / Leverage 5 => composite 4.3 => candidate feature.

Shortlist: candidate features (ranked, brief description, quick owner suggestion)
1) Preserve KV-cache across routing fallbacks (composite 4.3) — owner: serving-runtime (SRE + runtime).
   - Why: customers with bursty traffic and fallback rules see 2–5x latency spikes on fallback; immediate user-facing pain.
   - Rough scope: prototype sticky cache token exchange + graceful warming.
2) API-level versioned rollout flag for embeddings (composite 4.1) — owner: hosted-api/product-hosted-api.
   - Why: customers want deterministic embedding versions for downstream similarity indexes.
   - Quick MVP: a header + metadata flag that pins embedding model id in responses.
3) Latency-at-percentile dashboard (cost correlated) (composite 4.0) — owner: console-and-rollouts/observability.
   - Why: teams want P95/P99 broken down by model/route/token-count; helps debug regressions post-rollout.
   - MVP: per-route P95/P99 with token-length buckets for last 72 hours.
4) Request preview + simulation mode in Console (composite 3.9) — owner: developer-experience.
   - Why: reduces friction for customers evaluating quantized / deduced models; lowers support load.
5) Auto-suggest batching profile per API key (composite 3.7) — owner: optimize/product-optimize.
   - Why: lowers per-token cost for mid-size customers without engineering effort.
6) First-class model-variant metadata contract (labels: quantized, fp16, seq-len) (composite 3.6) — owner: product-hosted-api/model-onboarding.
7) Canary traffic weight quick rollback action (composite 3.5) — owner: console-and-rollouts.
8) Simple per-customer fallback policy templates (composite 3.5) — owner: solutions-engineering-and-professional-services.

Low-effort probes (fast experiments, 1–3 weeks)
- Probe A: "Sticky warm start" pilot for 3 enterprise customers — small runtime shim that preserves KV-cache across fallbacks for single-customer pilots. Measurable metric: P95 latency during fallback over 2 weeks.
- Probe B: Console flag: "pin-embedding-v1" — expose header and sample SDK change for one major customer. Measure: number of incidents due to embedding drift in 30 days.
- Probe C: Token-length percentile breakouts in an email report for top 10 customers — quick table export to test demand before building dashboard.

Risk flags / dependencies:
- KV-cache preservation requires runtime-level changes and may interact with privacy/isolation controls in Dedicated pools (dependency: security review).
- Embedding-version pinning needs coordination with model catalog and billing semantics (billing team + product).
- Some requests (long tail) are ambiguous: need to capture exact repro steps in ticket to avoid wasted effort.

Mapping to existing tickets & provenance (examples):
- CS-4122: "Fallback spike observed during EU outage" -> maps to KV-cache preservation proposal.
- CS-3988: "Embedding mismatch after model swap" -> maps to versioned embedding proposal.
- SE-607: Solutions note describing customer wants for batching helps prioritize Auto-suggest batching profile.

Suggested next steps (concrete):
1) Share this note with product leads (Serving Runtime PM, Hosted API PM, Optimize PM) and schedule a 30-minute triage session (owners listed).
2) Ask SRE/runtime to run a 1-hour feasibility sketch for KV-cache sticky warm start (deliverable: rough design + one blocker list).
3) Run the three low-effort probes in parallel where possible and report metrics in next CS sync (4 weeks).
4) Convert top-3 candidates to RFCs (2–4 page) with acceptance criteria and rollout plan.

Open questions for the triage session:
- What are acceptable privacy/isolation boundaries for sharing KV-cache across route variants?
- For embedding pinning, what billing/versioning semantics do we expose? (explicit pin vs. snapshot).
- Can we re-use existing tracing hooks for per-request token-length bucketing, or is a small instrumentation change required?

Appendix — selected customer vignettes (verbatim snippets):
- "We saw a 3x delay whenever we failover to dedicated during peak. That spike breaks our realtime flow." — Telco customer (support thread CS-4122).
- "After the model swap, our similarity index exploded. We need a way to freeze embeddings between runs." — Market research platform (CS-3988).
- "We'd pay a small premium if you provided automatic batching recommendations by API key — saves our infra people time." — Fintech startup (internal note from AE).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally operational and lean; aim is to create a bias toward action.
- Please annotate the doc in-line with objections or additional tickets to fold into the evidence pool.
